neighbours.label: being directed: the passive verb whose subject receives an instruction, permission, teaching or assignment (be asked to, were taught, was allowed to, was sent), against active voice
fire: At the border, every passenger was asked to show a ticket and a passport.
As apprentices we were taught to sharpen the chisels before each job.
After six months the hostages were allowed to write to their families.
The young officer was sent to a remote outpost near the border.
New employees are instructed to change their passwords on the first day.
At the meeting, residents were told that the bridge would close in May.
The patient was advised to rest and avoid lifting anything heavy.
During the strike, the drivers were ordered to return to the depot.
quiet: At the border, the guard checked every ticket and passport by hand.
As apprentices we sharpened the chisels before each job.
After six months the hostages wrote long letters to their families.
The young officer drove to a remote outpost near the border.
New employees change their passwords on the first day.
At the meeting, the mayor explained that the bridge would close in May.
The patient rested and avoided lifting anything heavy.
During the strike, the drivers returned to the depot.
